title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-20
lineage: Master Reel > ? > R @ 7.5 ips > CD > EAC > WAV > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Cleaned‑up soundboard tape captures a solid early‑1970 show, highlighted by a scorching Viola Lee Blues and a fiery Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The new SBD transfer removes much of the original hiss and separates the instruments enough to make this classic early‑70 performance enjoyable, though occasional distortion and low Pig Pen organ levels keep it from being perfect. Musically the show is above average – the acoustic set shines with Deep Elem Blues and Friend of the Devil, while the electric portion delivers a blistering Viola Lee Blues and an unforgettable Lovelight rap.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the show’s musical moments and note significant improvement in the tape transfer, but several point out lingering distortion and mix issues, yielding an overall above‑average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hiss reduced and instruments better separated after new transfer; occasional tape distortion and low Pig Pen organ level; vocals sometimes dominate the mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong acoustic half with flawless Deep Elem Blues and a unique Friend of the Devil rendition, followed by an electric set that builds intensity toward a blazing Viola Lee Blues and a memorable Lovelight rap.

band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh sings loudly and on‑key with his high harmonies, though they are often buried in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig Pen's organ is low in the mix, making his contributions less audible despite a lively rap during Lovelight.
